learning_outcomes.text: Understand crystal structure, deformation mechanisms and strengthening mechanisms in metals
Understand the use of phase diagrams to predict the equilibrium structure of metals and alloys
Develop a basic knowledge of heat treatment of metals
Understand the properties on non-metallic materials
Appreciate the importance of environmental factors and sustainability

syllabus_topics: Measurement of mechanical properties of materials
Atomic bonding and crystal structure of solids
Crystal defects and effects on properties
Phase diagrams and microstructure of metals and alloys
Non-metallic materials including ceramics, polymers and composites
teaching_methods: Online learning (short, pre-recorded videos and directed reading and study)
assessment_rules: Students must gain a summative mark of 40% to pass the module. Students who fail the module at the first attempt will be re-assessed during the July/August exam diet. This re-assessment will consist entirely of a 2-hour written examination. No marks from any previous attempts will be transferred to a new resit attempt.
bibliography: “Materials Science and Engineering: an Introduction” by Wm D Callister, John Wiley & Sons, 2003, ISBN 0-471-22471-S
Additional online textbooks will be referenced through Myplace.
